--[[
AchaeaTalismans - see how far your talisman pieces get you.
It reads what the game prints for six TALISMAN listings, keeps it, and draws a window from it:
TALISMAN PIECES what you hold, grouped by talisman TALISMAN PIECES <t> the same for one talisman TALISMAN INFO <t> what a talisman is built from TALISMAN SET <set> which talismans a set holds TALISMAN SETS every set, and how many of each you have done TALISMAN LIST the same sets, plus the talismans you have done
Nothing has to be typed differently: the package reads those whenever they are typed, by you or by `tals scan`. Reading is all it does unless asked to scan, and a scan sends only TALISMAN commands, plus MORE while the listing it is waiting for is paged. What a scan is answered with is read and kept off the screen: the window is where it shows.
The arithmetic is HELP TALISMANS (19.24): "Two Pieces of the same level may be combined into a Piece of one level higher", and split back down. So a piece at level n is worth 2^(n-1) level-1 pieces, and a slot that asks for level 7 wants 64 of those. Every piece you hold of a slot's keyword counts toward it, whatever its level, because a higher one can be split down and lower ones combined up. A slot is ready when the sum reaches what it asks for; the COMBINE and SPLIT commands that get it there are still yours to type.
tals show the window, and what has been read so far tals show|hide the window tals all the window lists every talisman you hold pieces of tals set <set> the window lists one set's talismans tals scan TALISMAN LIST and PIECES, SET for every set, then INFO for each talisman you hold pieces of and have not read tals scan <set> TALISMAN SET <set> and PIECES, then INFO for each of its talismans tals stop stop a scan tals diag build stamp, what is stored, where
]]
AchaeaTalismans = AchaeaTalismans or {} local M = AchaeaTalismans
M.VERSION = "0.4.0" M.BUILD = M.BUILD or "source" -- build.py replaces this
-- The name Mudlet knows the package by, which is what its uninstall event -- carries. build.py has the same string; the harness holds the two together. M.PACKAGE = "AchaeaTalismans" M.WINDOW = "AchaeaTalismans"
-- ------------------------------------------------------------------- the data
-- Everything saved, and the type each key must have to come back from a -- file. A key not listed here is neither saved nor loaded, so the two cannot -- disagree. local DATA_KEYS = { sets = "table", -- keyword -> { name, done, total, talismans } setOrder = "table", -- set keywords, in the game's order talismans = "table", -- keyword -> { name, brief, set, pieces } held = "table", -- the last TALISMAN PIECES, one row per line heldAt = "number", -- when that was read, os.time(); 0 for never completed = "table", -- talisman keyword -> { name, set } focus = "string", -- the set the window shows, or "" for all held shown = "boolean", -- whether the window is open piecesOpen = "boolean", -- whether the pieces held are listed or folded to a line openTalismans = "table", -- talisman keyword -> true, for those listing their pieces }
local function fresh() return { sets = {}, setOrder = {}, talismans = {}, held = {}, heldAt = 0, completed = {}, focus = "", shown = true, piecesOpen = false, openTalismans = {}, } end
M.data = M.data or fresh()
-- On the module table rather than in a file-local: Mudlet keeps temp triggers -- and timers across a script recompile, and a fresh local would lose the ids -- of the old ones and install a second set. M.state = M.state or { triggers = {}, handlers = {}, cap = nil, -- the output being read, if any scan = nil, -- the scan in progress, if any answered = false, -- the scan answered the page break now showing tailUntil = 0, -- until when the lines after a scan's listing are its own loaded = "none", read = 0, -- outputs read since the package started } local S = M.state
local function log(message, colour) local text = "\n<" .. (colour or "gold") .. ">[tals]<reset> " .. message .. "\n" -- Echo inside a trigger goes into the line that fired it, line feeds and -- all (Mudlet 5.1's TConsoleModel::echo), so deleting that line, as a scan -- does, takes the message with it. From a trigger it is printed once the -- trigger is done, on a line of its own. if S.inFeed then tempTimer(0, function() -- By then the lines a scan hid are gone, and the window may already -- end on an empty line: the leading newline would add a blank one. cecho(M.lastLineEmpty() and text:sub(2) or text) end) else cecho(text) end end
function M.now() if type(getEpoch) == "function" then local ok, t = pcall(getEpoch) if ok and type(t) == "number" then return t end end return os.time() end
--- Whether the main window's last line is empty. getLineCount is the last --- line's index and getLines(from, to) stops short of `to`, both in 5.0.1 --- and 5.1.0, so this is that line alone. function M.lastLineEmpty() if type(getLineCount) ~= "function" or type(getLines) ~= "function" then return false end local ok, last = pcall(function() local n = getLineCount() return getLines(n, n + 1)[1] end) return ok and last == "" end
-- ---------------------------------------------------------- saving, loading
function M.path() return getMudletHomeDir() .. "/achaea-talismans.lua" end
function M.load() -- A recompile keeps M.data, which an older version may have made without -- a key added since; with no file to read, nothing else would add it. for key, value in pairs(fresh()) do if M.data[key] == nil then M.data[key] = value end end local path = M.path() if not (io.exists and io.exists(path)) then S.loaded = "none" return false end local stored = {} if not pcall(table.load, path, stored) then -- table.load runs the file as Lua, so a half-written one raises. Say so, -- and let M.save move it aside rather than write over it. S.loaded = "unreadable" log("could not read " .. path .. "; starting empty", "red") return false end local data = fresh() for key, kind in pairs(DATA_KEYS) do if type(stored[key]) == kind then data[key] = stored[key] end end M.data = data S.loaded = "ok" return true end
function M.save() local path = M.path() if S.loaded == "unreadable" then -- os.rename reports failure by returning nil, not by raising. If the file -- could not be moved aside, writing now would destroy the only copy. local ok, moved = pcall(os.rename, path, path .. ".bad") if not (ok and moved) then log("could not move " .. path .. " aside; nothing saved", "red") return false end S.loaded = "ok" end local out = {} for key in pairs(DATA_KEYS) do out[key] = M.data[key] end -- table.save reports a file it could not open by returning nil and a -- message, not by raising. So the message is the sign of a failure, and -- pcall's own result is not one. local ok, _, failed = pcall(table.save, path, out) if not ok or failed ~= nil then log("could not write " .. path .. "; what was read lasts until Mudlet closes", "red") return false end return true end
-- ------------------------------------------------------- reading the output
-- Every pattern below is written against a capture of the game's own output, -- typed on 2026-11-16 except where it says otherwise, and applied to a line -- with its trailing spaces removed: the game pads its header lines.
M.HEADERS = { -- TALISMAN PIECES. No indent before Num. pieces = "^Num%s+Name%s+Level%s+Set%s+Keyword$", -- TALISMAN PIECES <talisman>. The same columns, indented. tpieces = "^%s+Num%s+Name%s+Level%s+Set%s+Keyword$", -- The talisman tables in TALISMAN LIST. tlist = "^Name%s+Set%s+Keyword$", -- TALISMAN SETS, and the sets table in TALISMAN LIST. sets = "^Name%s+Status%s+Keyword$", } -- TALISMAN SET and TALISMAN INFO both open with this; the line after it says -- which one it is. M.NAME_LINE = "^Name: (.+)$" -- The tables open and close with a rule of dashes, 79 or 82 long. Twenty is -- enough to tell it from the underlines of a help scroll's headings. M.RULE = "^%-%-%-%-%-%-%-%-%-%-%-%-%-%-%-%-%-%-%-%-+$" -- The pager. Everything from the first line to the second is the client -- paging, and whatever arrived meanwhile is not part of the table. M.MORE_OPEN = "^%[Type MORE if you wish to continue reading" M.MORE_CLOSE = "^%[File continued via MORE%]" -- A paged table nobody went on reading is let go after this long, so that a -- later MORE for something else does not feed that something to it. M.PAUSE_MAX = 300 -- What a scan's listing may still print after its table or its last row, -- before the prompt that ends it, besides blank lines and another table. M.TAIL_LINES = { "^You have no incomplete talismans to show%.$", -- TALISMAN LIST } -- The rest of a listing comes with it, in the same packet or the next. A -- tail never closed by a prompt (a client that does not mark prompts) is let -- go after this long, so it cannot hide a listing typed later. M.TAIL_WAIT = 1
-- B 1 a Black Dragon's heart 1 Dragon blackdragonheart -- The name column is cut at 33 characters, so the name is taken as whatever -- comes before the last three columns rather than by width. M.ROW_PIECES = "^(%u) (%d+)%s+(.-)%s+(%d+)%s+(%S+)%s+(%S+)$" -- blackdragonpieces M.ROW_GROUP = "^%s%s%s%s%s%s(%S+)$" -- B (1) a Silver Dragon's claw 2 dragon silverdragonclaw M.ROW_TPIECES = "^%s+(%u) %((%d+)%) (.-)%s+(%d+)%s+(%S+)%s+(%S+)$" -- a miniature Air Elemental elemental airelemental M.ROW_TLIST = "^(.-)%s+(%S+)%s+(%S+)$" -- Dragon 0/6 dragon M.ROW_SETS = "^(.-)%s+(%d+)/(%d+)%s+(%S+)$" -- a Black Dragon Talisman (blackdragon) M.ROW_SET = "^(.-) %((%S+)%)$" -- (1) a Red Dragon's claw (reddragonclaw), level 7 -- A long one wraps, with the rest on the next line indented two spaces -- (INFO harness, 2026-10-15), so rows are joined before this is applied. M.ROW_INFO = "^%((%d+)%) (.-) %((%S+)%), level (%d+)$"
local function rtrim(s) return (s:gsub("%s+$", "")) end local function trim(s) return (s:gsub("^%s+", ""):gsub("%s+$", "")) end
local function headerKind(l) for kind, pattern in pairs(M.HEADERS) do if l:find(pattern) then return kind end end if l:find(M.NAME_LINE) then return "name" end return nil end
-- Each reader takes a capture and a line and answers with one of: -- nil the line was taken, keep reading -- "done" the line was taken and the output is over -- "pass" the output ended before this line, which is someone else's -- "drop" this was not the output it looked like local READ = {}
-- How far past its header's Keyword column a row's keyword may start: room -- for a set name a few characters wider than its column, and no more. M.KW_SLACK = 4
--- Whether a row's last field is a keyword where the header puts keywords. --- In every row of every table captured, the keyword is lower-case letters --- and digits and starts exactly in the Keyword column. A few columns later --- is allowed, for a set name wider than its column that pushed it right. --- A tell, a channel line or a timing tag that arrives mid-table almost never --- ends in such a word at such a place, so it is not taken as a row. local function inColumn(cap, l, kw) local col = cap.kwCol if not (col and kw and kw:find("^[%l%d]+$")) then return false end local start = #l - #kw + 1 return start >= col and start <= col + M.KW_SLACK and l:sub(start - 1, start - 1) == " " end
local function tableReader(onRow) return function(cap, l) if l:find(M.RULE) then if cap.rules == 0 then cap.rules, cap.ruleLen = 1, #l return nil end -- The closing rule is as long as the opening one; any other run of -- dashes is something else's. if #l == cap.ruleLen then return "done" end return nil end -- Before the opening rule nothing else is expected. if cap.rules == 0 then return "drop" end -- A line inside the table that is neither a row nor a heading, a tell -- above all, is taken so the table goes on, but is not the table's. cap.foreign = not onRow(cap, l) return nil end end
READ.pieces = tableReader(function(cap, l) local src, n, name, level, set, kw = l:match(M.ROW_PIECES) if src and inColumn(cap, l, kw) then cap.rows[#cap.rows + 1] = { source = src, count = tonumber(n), name = trim(name), level = tonumber(level), set = set, kw = kw, group = cap.group, } return true end local heading = l:match(M.ROW_GROUP) if heading then -- The heading is the talisman's keyword with "pieces" on the end, as far -- as the six dragons show; the others are read the same way. cap.group = heading:gsub("pieces$", "") return true end return false end)
READ.tpieces = tableReader(function(cap, l) local src, n, name, level, set, kw = l:match(M.ROW_TPIECES) if src and inColumn(cap, l, kw) then cap.rows[#cap.rows + 1] = { source = src, count = tonumber(n), name = trim(name), level = tonumber(level), set = set, kw = kw, } return true end return false end)
READ.tlist = tableReader(function(cap, l) local name, set, kw = l:match(M.ROW_TLIST) if name and name ~= "" and inColumn(cap, l, kw) then cap.rows[#cap.rows + 1] = { name = trim(name), set = set, kw = kw } return true end return false end)
READ.sets = tableReader(function(cap, l) local name, done, total, kw = l:match(M.ROW_SETS) if name and inColumn(cap, l, kw) then cap.rows[#cap.rows + 1] = { name = trim(name), done = tonumber(done), total = tonumber(total), kw = kw, } return true end return false end)
-- The line after "Name:" decides between a set and a talisman. READ.name = function(cap, l) local partial = l:match("^Partial name: (%S+)$") if partial then cap.kind, cap.kw, cap.rows = "set", partial, {} return nil end local kw = l:match("^Keyword: (%S+)$") if kw then cap.kind, cap.kw, cap.pieces = "info", kw, {} return nil end return "drop" end
READ.set = function(cap, l) if cap.listing then local name, kw = l:match(M.ROW_SET) if name then cap.rows[#cap.rows + 1] = { name = name, kw = kw } return nil end return "pass" end if l == "Talismans:" then cap.listing = true; return nil end local desc = l:match("^Description: (.*)$") if desc then cap.description = desc; return nil end if l:find("^ ") and cap.description then cap.description = cap.description .. " " .. trim(l) return nil end return "pass" end
local function flushPiece(cap) if not cap.pending then return end local n, name, kw, level = cap.pending:match(M.ROW_INFO) if n then cap.pieces[#cap.pieces + 1] = { count = tonumber(n), name = name, kw = kw, level = tonumber(level), } else cap.unread = (cap.unread or 0) + 1 end cap.pending = nil end
READ.info = function(cap, l) local set = l:match("^Set: (.*)$") if set then flushPiece(cap) cap.set = trim(set) return "done" end if l == "Pieces:" then cap.listing = true; return nil end local brief = l:match("^Brief: (.*)$") if brief then cap.brief = brief; return nil end if l:find("^ ") then if cap.pending then cap.pending = cap.pending .. " " .. trim(l) elseif cap.brief and not cap.listing then cap.brief = cap.brief .. " " .. trim(l) end return nil end if cap.listing and l:find("^%(%d+%) ") then flushPiece(cap) cap.pending = l return nil end flushPiece(cap) return "pass" end
-- -------------------------------------------------- folding what was read in
--- The set keyword for a set as some listing names it: TALISMAN PIECES says --- "Dragon", TALISMAN PIECES <t> says "dragon", TALISMAN INFO says "Dragon", --- and Miscellaneous's keyword is "misc". function M.setKey(name) if not name then return nil end local low = name:lower() if M.data.sets[low] then return low end for kw, set in pairs(M.data.sets) do if (set.name or ""):lower() == low then return kw end end return low end
--- Which talisman a piece keyword belongs to: TALISMAN INFO says for certain, --- and failing that the heading it was last listed under. function M.ownerOf(pieceKw) for tkw, t in pairs(M.data.talismans) do for _, p in ipairs(t.pieces or {}) do if p.kw == pieceKw then return tkw end end end for _, row in ipairs(M.data.held) do if row.kw == pieceKw and row.group then return row.group end end return nil end
local COMMIT = {}
COMMIT.pieces = function(cap) M.data.held = cap.rows M.data.heldAt = os.time() end
-- One talisman's pieces replace what was held for that talisman, and only -- that. Which talisman is worked out from the rows, since the output does -- not name it. COMMIT.tpieces = function(cap) local owner, mixed = nil, false for _, row in ipairs(cap.rows) do local o = M.ownerOf(row.kw) if o == nil or (owner and o ~= owner) then mixed = true end owner = owner or o row.group = o end -- Nothing read so far says whose pieces these are, but the command that -- was typed for them does. local asked = S.asked local named = asked and M.now() - asked.at < M.ASKED_FOR and M.resolveTalisman(asked.kw) if (owner == nil or mixed) and named then owner, mixed = named, false for _, row in ipairs(cap.rows) do row.group = row.group or owner end end M.data.heldAt = os.time() local gone = {} if owner and not mixed then for _, row in ipairs(M.data.held) do if row.group == owner then gone[row] = true end end else local kws = {} for _, row in ipairs(cap.rows) do kws[row.kw] = true end for _, row in ipairs(M.data.held) do if kws[row.kw] then gone[row] = true end end end local held, placed = {}, false for _, row in ipairs(M.data.held) do if gone[row] then if not placed then for _, new in ipairs(cap.rows) do held[#held + 1] = new end placed = true end else held[#held + 1] = row end end if not placed then for _, new in ipairs(cap.rows) do held[#held + 1] = new end end M.data.held = held end
-- HELP TALISMANS says TALISMAN LIST shows the completed talismans and the -- completed ones you carry, and in the one LIST captured both come straight -- before the sets table, untitled, with the incomplete ones after it. So a -- talisman table counts as done only when a sets table follows it within a -- few lines (S.listed, below); one that comes after, or on its own, does -- not, because nothing says what it lists. Done is added to, never cleared. COMMIT.tlist = function(cap) S.listed = S.listed or {} for _, row in ipairs(cap.rows) do S.listed[#S.listed + 1] = row end end
COMMIT.sets = function(cap) for _, row in ipairs(cap.done or {}) do M.data.completed[row.kw] = { name = row.name, set = row.set } end local order = {} for _, row in ipairs(cap.rows) do local set = M.data.sets[row.kw] if not set then -- A set read by TALISMAN SET before SETS was ever read went in under -- the keyword SET printed, which may not be this one: take it over. for kw, other in pairs(M.data.sets) do if kw ~= row.kw and (other.name or ""):lower() == row.name:lower() then set = other M.data.sets[kw] = nil break end end end set = set or {} set.name, set.done, set.total = row.name, row.done, row.total M.data.sets[row.kw] = set order[#order + 1] = row.kw end M.data.setOrder = order end
COMMIT.set = function(cap) local key = M.data.sets[cap.kw] and cap.kw or nil if not key then for kw, set in pairs(M.data.sets) do if (set.name or ""):lower() == cap.name:lower() then key = kw; break end end end key = key or cap.kw cap.key = key local set = M.data.sets[key] or {} set.name = cap.name set.talismans = cap.rows set.description = cap.description M.data.sets[key] = set for _, kw in ipairs(M.data.setOrder) do if kw == key then return end end M.data.setOrder[#M.data.setOrder + 1] = key end
COMMIT.info = function(cap) M.data.talismans[cap.kw] = { name = cap.name, brief = cap.brief, set = cap.set, pieces = cap.pieces, } end
function M.commit(cap) if not COMMIT[cap.kind] then return false end COMMIT[cap.kind](cap) S.read = S.read + 1 M.save() M.scanHeard(cap) M.redraw() return true end
--- Whether the scan is waiting for a listing that opens this way. local function scanWants(kind) local step = S.scan and S.scan.step if not step then return false end if kind == "name" then return step.kind == "set" or step.kind == "info" end return step.kind == kind or (step.kinds and step.kinds[kind]) or false end
local function open(l) local kind = headerKind(l) if not kind then return end if kind == "name" then S.cap = { kind = "name", name = l:match(M.NAME_LINE) } else S.cap = { kind = kind, rules = 0, rows = {}, kwCol = l:find("Keyword", 1, true) } end S.cap.fromScan = scanWants(kind) -- Hidden: the scan's own, or a table that follows one of the scan's in the -- same output, as LIST's incomplete talismans follow its sets table. S.cap.hide = S.cap.fromScan or M.inTail() -- Talisman tables count as done only if a sets table follows them with -- nothing but blank lines between (M.feed lets them go otherwise). if kind == "sets" then S.cap.done, S.listed = S.listed, nil elseif kind ~= "tlist" then S.listed = nil end end
--- Whether the line now in the trigger is a prompt. Mudlet knows from the --- game's GA; without it, nothing is taken for one. local function atPrompt() if type(isPrompt) ~= "function" then return false end local ok, yes = pcall(isPrompt) return ok and yes == true end
--- Whether lines are still arriving after a scan's listing, before its prompt. function M.inTail() return (S.tailUntil or 0) > 0 and M.now() <= S.tailUntil end
local function startTail() S.tailUntil = M.now() + M.TAIL_WAIT end local function endTail() S.tailUntil = 0 end
--- What follows a scan's listing up to its prompt: blank lines, the lines in --- M.TAIL_LINES, and the prompt, which ends it. Anything else ends it too, --- and is shown. local function tail(l) if not M.inTail() then return false end if atPrompt() then endTail(); return true end if l == "" then return true end for _, pattern in ipairs(M.TAIL_LINES) do if l:find(pattern) then return true end end endTail() return false end
--- One line of game output. Everything the package knows comes through here. --- True when the line is part of what a scan was answered with, which the --- trigger then deletes: a scan is read, not watched. A line the package --- cannot place in a scan's listing, a tell above all, is always left. function M.feed(text) local l = rtrim(text or "") local cap = S.cap if l:find(M.MORE_OPEN) then S.paging, S.answered = true, false if cap and cap.paused then -- A second page break before the first was read on: the pager is -- showing something else now, and this listing was left unfinished. S.cap = nil elseif cap then cap.paused, cap.pausedAt = true, M.now() -- Answered only for a listing the scan asked for and is waiting on. if cap.fromScan and S.scan then send("more", false); S.answered = true end elseif S.between and S.scan and S.scan.step then -- Straight after one of the scan's tables closed, with nothing but -- blank lines since, and the scan still waiting on the same step: the -- break falls between two tables of its listing, as LIST's are. send("more", false) S.answered = true end return S.answered end if l:find(M.MORE_CLOSE) then local ours = S.answered S.paging, S.answered = false, false if cap and cap.paused then if M.now() - (cap.pausedAt or 0) > M.PAUSE_MAX then S.cap = nil else cap.paused = false end end return ours end -- What the pager let in between pages is not part of any output. A new -- listing's header means the pager was left, so it ends that, and drops a -- listing that was waiting on a page. if S.paging then -- The page's own prompt, when the scan answered it, is the scan's. if not headerKind(l) then return S.answered and atPrompt() end S.paging, S.answered = false, false if cap and cap.paused then S.cap, cap = nil, nil end end -- Between two of the scan's tables only until something else is printed. if l ~= "" then S.between = false end -- In LIST the sets table follows the done talismans after one blank line. -- Any other line between, a prompt above all, means they were not one -- listing. if S.listed and not cap and l ~= "" and not headerKind(l) then S.listed = nil end -- A new listing starting means a table or a paged output was never -- finished, and it is let go. An unpaged SET or INFO is left to its reader, -- which ends it on any line it does not know. if cap and (cap.rules or cap.paused) and headerKind(l) then S.cap, cap = nil, nil end if cap and cap.paused then return false end if cap then local verdict = READ[cap.kind](cap, l) if verdict == nil then -- "Name:" opens SET and INFO alike, and only the line after says which, -- and for INFO which talisman. One the scan did not ask for, typed or -- otherwise, is shown from here on. Its "Name:" line was already hidden -- and cannot be put back. if cap.hide and not cap.claimed and (cap.kind == "set" or cap.kind == "info") then cap.claimed = true if not M.scanWaitsFor(cap) then cap.hide, cap.fromScan = false, false end end local foreign = cap.foreign cap.foreign = nil return cap.hide and not foreign or false end S.cap = nil if verdict == "done" then local step = S.scan and S.scan.step -- Before the commit, which may end the scan: what follows this listing -- in its output is still the scan's. if cap.hide then startTail() end M.commit(cap) -- A scan table closed, and the scan has not moved on: more of its -- listing may follow, after a page break. if cap.fromScan and cap.rules and step and S.scan and S.scan.step == step then S.between = true end return cap.hide or false end if verdict == "pass" then if cap.hide then startTail() end M.commit(cap) end -- "pass" and "drop" both leave this line to be looked at afresh. A -- dropped listing's first line is gone if it was hidden: it looked like -- the scan's answer, and was not. It cannot be put back. end open(l) if S.cap then return S.cap.hide or false end return tail(l) end
-- ------------------------------------------------------------- the arithmetic
--- A piece at this level, in level-1 pieces. function M.units(level) return 2 ^ ((tonumber(level) or 1) - 1) end
--- Every held piece of this keyword, in level-1 pieces. function M.heldUnits(pieceKw) local n = 0 for _, row in ipairs(M.data.held) do if row.kw == pieceKw then n = n + row.count * M.units(row.level) end end return n end
local function label(tkw, pieceKw) if pieceKw:sub(1, #tkw) == tkw and #pieceKw > #tkw then return pieceKw:sub(#tkw + 1) end return pieceKw end
--- How far the pieces held get one talisman, from its TALISMAN INFO. function M.progress(tkw) local t = M.data.talismans[tkw] if not t then return nil end local slots, ready, have, need = {}, 0, 0, 0 for _, p in ipairs(t.pieces or {}) do local want = p.count * M.units(p.level) local got = M.heldUnits(p.kw) local counted = math.min(got, want) slots[#slots + 1] = { kw = p.kw, label = label(tkw, p.kw), level = p.level, count = p.count, have = got, need = want, } if got >= want then ready = ready + 1 end have, need = have + counted, need + want end return { slots = slots, ready = ready, have = have, need = need } end
--- "done", "started" or "none". function M.status(tkw) if M.data.completed[tkw] then return "done" end local t = M.data.talismans[tkw] for _, row in ipairs(M.data.held) do if row.group == tkw then return "started" end if t then for _, p in ipairs(t.pieces or {}) do if p.kw == row.kw then return "started" end end end end return "none" end
--- Talisman keywords you hold pieces of, in the order TALISMAN PIECES listed --- them. function M.heldTalismans() local out, seen = {}, {} for _, row in ipairs(M.data.held) do local tkw = row.group or M.ownerOf(row.kw) if tkw and not seen[tkw] then seen[tkw] = true out[#out + 1] = tkw end end return out end
-- -------------------------------------------------------------- the drawing
M.BAR = 10 -- Spaces between two columns of the layout. M.GAP = 3 -- The fewest marks a line of a set may hold before the sets go to one column. M.MIN_MARKS = 4 -- The width drawn to when the window cannot be measured. M.DEFAULT_WIDTH = 80 local MARK = { done = "<green>●", started = "<yellow>◐", none = "<dim_grey>○" }
local function bar(have, need) local fill = need > 0 and math.floor(M.BAR * math.min(have, need) / need) or 0 if have > 0 and fill == 0 then fill = 1 end local colour = have >= need and "<green>" or (have > 0 and "<yellow>" or "<dim_grey>") return colour .. string.rep("█", fill) .. "<dim_grey>" .. string.rep("░", M.BAR - fill) end
local function pad(s, n) if #s >= n then return s:sub(1, n) end return s .. string.rep(" ", n - #s) end
local function fmt(n) return string.format("%d", n) end
-- A link's code is a string of Lua that Mudlet compiles when it is clicked, -- and the keywords in it come from the game or from what was typed, so each -- goes in as a quoted literal rather than pasted between quote marks. local function q(s) return string.format("%q", s) end
--- How many columns a piece of cecho text takes on screen: its colour tags --- take none, and a bar or a mark is one column however many bytes it is. function M.textWidth(s) s = s:gsub("<[%w_,:]+>", "") local _, n = s:gsub("[^\128-\191]", "") return n end
-- A line is a list of pieces, as M.render returns them, with its width in w. local function newLine() return { w = 0 } end local function put(line, s) line[#line + 1] = s line.w = line.w + M.textWidth(s) return line end local function putLink(line, text, code, hint) line[#line + 1] = { text, code, hint } line.w = line.w + M.textWidth(text) return line end local BLANK = newLine()
-- How many blank lines go between a block and the one under it: sep, or -- more if the block above asks for more with its own `after`. local function gapAfter(b, sep) return math.max(sep, b.after or 0) end
-- Stack the blocks, in order, into columns no taller than height, with the -- gap above between two blocks in one column, and none at a column's foot. -- A block is never split. local function stack(blocks, height, sep) local cols, col = {}, nil for i, b in ipairs(blocks) do local gap = i > 1 and gapAfter(blocks[i - 1], sep) or 0 if col and #col + gap + #b <= height then for _ = 1, gap do col[#col + 1] = BLANK end else col = { w = 0 } cols[#cols + 1] = col end for _, l in ipairs(b) do col[#col + 1] = l if l.w > col.w then col.w = l.w end end end return cols end
--- Lay blocks of lines out in columns read top to bottom, as many as fit in --- width, each as wide as its widest line. The shortest layout that fits wins; --- one wider than the window is a single column. function M.layout(blocks, width, sep) local tallest, total = 0, 0 for i, b in ipairs(blocks) do if #b > tallest then tallest = #b end total = total + #b + (i > 1 and gapAfter(blocks[i - 1], sep) or 0) end for height = tallest, total do local cols = stack(blocks, height, sep) local w = M.GAP * (#cols - 1) for _, col in ipairs(cols) do w = w + col.w end if w <= width then return cols end end return stack(blocks, total, sep) end
--- Lay blocks out in at most n columns read top to bottom, as short as that --- allows. Blocks are never split, so a column may come out a line longer --- than the other. function M.layoutInto(blocks, n, sep) local tallest, total = 0, 0 for i, b in ipairs(blocks) do if #b > tallest then tallest = #b end total = total + #b + (i > 1 and gapAfter(blocks[i - 1], sep) or 0) end for height = tallest, total do local cols = stack(blocks, height, sep) if #cols <= n then return cols end end return stack(blocks, total, sep) end
--- Emit columns row by row into out, padding each cell to its column's width. function M.emit(out, cols) local rows = 0 for _, col in ipairs(cols) do if #col > rows then rows = #col end end for r = 1, rows do local last = 0 for c, col in ipairs(cols) do if col[r] and col[r].w > 0 then last = c end end for c = 1, last do local line = cols[c][r] or BLANK out[#out + 1] = "<reset>" for _, piece in ipairs(line) do out[#out + 1] = piece end if c < last then out[#out + 1] = string.rep(" ", cols[c].w - line.w + M.GAP) end end out[#out + 1] = "\n" end end
-- One talisman: its name and how far along it is, then, when it is open, a -- row per piece. A talisman with rows to show is folded to its name until -- clicked, so a long list stays a list of names. local function talismanBlock(tkw) local d = M.data local t = d.talismans[tkw] local status = M.status(tkw) local p = M.progress(tkw) local rows = {} if status == "done" then -- Nothing left to show. elseif p then local lw, vw = 1, 1 for _, s in ipairs(p.slots) do s.lvl = (s.count > 1 and (fmt(s.count) .. "x") or "") .. "L" .. fmt(s.level) lw = math.max(lw, math.min(#s.label, 16)) vw = math.max(vw, #s.lvl) end for _, s in ipairs(p.slots) do rows[#rows + 1] = put(newLine(), " <reset>" .. pad(s.label, lw) .. " <dim_grey>" .. pad(s.lvl, vw) .. " " .. bar(s.have, s.need) .. " <reset>" .. fmt(s.have) .. "/" .. fmt(s.need)) end else for _, row in ipairs(d.held) do if row.group == tkw then rows[#rows + 1] = put(newLine(), " <reset>" .. label(tkw, row.kw) .. " <dim_grey>" .. fmt(row.count) .. " at L" .. fmt(row.level) .. " = " .. fmt(row.count * M.units(row.level))) end end end
local open = #rows > 0 and d.openTalismans[tkw] and true or false local name = MARK[status] .. " <white>" .. (t and t.name or tkw) local head = newLine() if #rows > 0 then putLink(head, (open and "<cyan>▾ " or "<cyan>▸ ") .. name, "AchaeaTalismans.toggleTalisman(" .. q(tkw) .. ")", open and "fold its pieces" or "list its pieces") else put(head, " " .. name) end put(head, "<reset> <dim_grey>(" .. tkw .. ")") if status == "done" then put(head, " <green>done") elseif p then local pct = p.need > 0 and math.floor(100 * p.have / p.need) or 0 put(head, " <reset>" .. fmt(p.ready) .. "/" .. fmt(#p.slots) .. " ready, " .. fmt(pct) .. "%") else put(head, " <dim_grey>needs not read ") putLink(head, "<cyan>[info]", "send(" .. q("talisman info " .. tkw) .. ", false)", "TALISMAN INFO " .. tkw) end
local block = { head } if open then for _, l in ipairs(rows) do block[#block + 1] = l end -- A blank line under an open talisman, to set it off from the next. block.after = 1 end return block end
--- The talismans the window lists: the focused set's, or, with no set --- focused, those you hold pieces of. function M.listed() local d = M.data if d.focus == "" then return M.heldTalismans() end local set = d.sets[d.focus] local list = {} if set and set.talismans then for _, t in ipairs(set.talismans) do list[#list + 1] = t.kw end else for tkw, t in pairs(d.talismans) do if M.setKey(t.set) == d.focus then list[#list + 1] = tkw end end table.sort(list) end return list end
--- What the window shows, laid out for a window this many columns wide, as --- a list of pieces: a string is coloured text, a table is { text, code, hint } --- and becomes a link that runs the code. function M.render(width) width = width or M.DEFAULT_WIDTH local out = {} local function add(s) out[#out + 1] = s end local function link(text, code, hint) out[#out + 1] = { text, code, hint } end local d = M.data
add("<white>Talisman pieces<reset>") if d.heldAt > 0 then add("<dim_grey> read " .. os.date("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M", d.heldAt) .. " ") else add("<dim_grey> pieces not read yet ") end link("<cyan>[scan]", "AchaeaTalismans.scan()", "send TALISMAN LIST, PIECES and SET for every set, then INFO for what you hold") add(" ") link("<cyan>[all]", "AchaeaTalismans.setFocus('')", "the pieces you hold, and every set") add("\n\n")
-- [open all] [fold all], beside a heading if they fit and under it if not. local ALL_WIDTH = #"[open all] [fold all]" local function openAll() link("<cyan>[open all]", "AchaeaTalismans.openAll(true)", "list every talisman's pieces") add(" ") link("<cyan>[fold all]", "AchaeaTalismans.openAll(false)", "fold every talisman to its name") end
local list if d.focus ~= "" then local set = d.sets[d.focus] local name = set and set.name or d.focus local done = (set and set.total) and (" " .. fmt(set.done) .. "/" .. fmt(set.total) .. " done") or "" add("<white>" .. name .. "<reset>" .. done .. " ") link("<cyan>[scan set]", "AchaeaTalismans.scan(" .. q(d.focus) .. ")", "send TALISMAN SET and PIECES, then INFO for each of its talismans") add(" ") link("<cyan>[back to sets]", "AchaeaTalismans.setFocus('')", "every talisman you hold pieces of, and every set") list = M.listed() if #list > 0 then local heading = M.textWidth(name .. done .. " [scan set] [back to sets]") add(heading + 1 + ALL_WIDTH <= width and " " or "\n") openAll() end add("\n") if #list == 0 then add("<dim_grey> its talismans are not read yet\n") end else list = M.heldTalismans() if #d.held == 0 then add("<dim_grey>No pieces read yet. TALISMAN PIECES, or [scan].\n") else -- Folded by default to one line, so the sets below are what shows. local whole = 0 for _, tkw in ipairs(list) do local p = M.status(tkw) ~= "done" and M.progress(tkw) if p and #p.slots > 0 and p.ready == #p.slots then whole = whole + 1 end end link((d.piecesOpen and "<cyan>▾ " or "<cyan>▸ ") .. "<white>Pieces you hold", "AchaeaTalismans.togglePieces()", d.piecesOpen and "fold the pieces you hold" or "list the pieces you hold") local pieces = 0 for _, row in ipairs(d.held) do pieces = pieces + row.count end local summary = " <dim_grey>" .. fmt(pieces) .. (pieces == 1 and " piece" or " pieces") .. (#list > 0 and (" of " .. fmt(#list) .. (#list == 1 and " talisman" or " talismans")) or "") .. (whole > 0 and (", " .. fmt(whole) .. " with every piece") or "") add(summary) if not d.piecesOpen then list = {} add("\n") else if #list > 0 then -- Beside the heading if they fit, else under it. local heading = M.textWidth("▾ Pieces you hold" .. summary) add(heading + 2 + ALL_WIDTH <= width and " " or "\n ") openAll() end add("\n\n") end end end
local blocks = {} for _, tkw in ipairs(list) do blocks[#blocks + 1] = talismanBlock(tkw) end if #blocks > 0 then if d.focus ~= "" then add("\n") end M.emit(out, M.layout(blocks, width, 0)) end
local loose = {} for _, row in ipairs(d.held) do if not (row.group or M.ownerOf(row.kw)) then loose[#loose + 1] = { put(newLine(), "<reset>" .. row.kw .. " <dim_grey>" .. fmt(row.count) .. " at L" .. fmt(row.level) .. " = " .. fmt(row.count * M.units(row.level))) } end end if d.focus == "" and d.piecesOpen and #loose > 0 then add("\n<white>Pieces of no known talisman<reset>\n") M.emit(out, M.layout(loose, width, 0)) end
-- One set is shown on its own: the window keeps to its bottom, so a sets -- list drawn under the set's talismans would push them out of sight. if d.focus ~= "" then return out elseif #d.setOrder > 0 then add("\n<white>Sets<reset> <dim_grey>click one to list its talismans\n") local nw = 1 for _, kw in ipairs(d.setOrder) do nw = math.max(nw, #(d.sets[kw].name or kw)) end -- Two columns, each half the window, and a set's marks wrap within its -- column, under the first of them, rather than widen it: the longest -- set has 19 talismans, and one wide row would make every row in its -- column as wide. A window too narrow to show a few marks a line in -- half of it gets one column of its full width instead. local lead = nw + 1 + 5 + 1 -- name, a space, the counts padded, a space local columns, colW = 2, math.floor((width - M.GAP) / 2) if colW - lead < M.MIN_MARKS then columns, colW = 1, width end local perLine = math.max(1, colW - lead) local blocks = {} for _, kw in ipairs(d.setOrder) do local set = d.sets[kw] local line = putLink(newLine(), "<reset>" .. pad(set.name or kw, nw), "AchaeaTalismans.setFocus(" .. q(kw) .. ")", "list the " .. (set.name or kw) .. " set") -- A set read by TALISMAN SET alone has no counts yet. local counts = set.total and (fmt(set.done or 0) .. "/" .. fmt(set.total)) or "?" local block = {} if set.talismans then put(line, " <dim_grey>" .. pad(counts, 5) .. " ") local marks = {} for _, t in ipairs(set.talismans) do marks[#marks + 1] = MARK[M.status(t.kw)] end local i = 1 repeat put(line, table.concat(marks, "", i, math.min(#marks, i + perLine - 1))) i = i + perLine block[#block + 1] = line if i <= #marks then line = put(newLine(), string.rep(" ", lead)) end until i > #marks else block[1] = put(line, " <dim_grey>" .. counts) end blocks[#blocks + 1] = block end M.emit(out, M.layoutInto(blocks, columns, 0)) else add("\n<dim_grey>Sets not read yet. TALISMAN SETS, or [scan].\n") end return out end
--- The width in pixels of one character cell in a window. 5.1 says exactly, --- with calcFontSize(win, true). 5.0 raises for that form, and its --- calcFontSize(win) is the width of a "W", the nearest it has. function M.cellWidth(win) if type(calcFontSize) ~= "function" then return nil end for _, args in ipairs({ { win, true }, { win } }) do local ok, w = pcall(calcFontSize, args[1], args[2]) if ok and type(w) == "number" and w > 0 then return w end end return nil end
--- How many columns the window can show, all of them in full. --- --- getColumnCount is not that. It is the window's width over the font's --- average character width as a fraction (QFontMetricsF), rounded, while --- every character is drawn in a cell as wide as that average rounded to a --- whole pixel (TTextEdit's mFontWidth, in 5.0.1 and 5.1.0 alike). With an --- average of 7.6 drawn at 8, it counts five columns in a hundred too many, --- and a layout fitted to it ran past the window's right edge. --- --- From what it does say: the width is at least (n - 0.5) averages, and the --- average is at least the cell less half a pixel. So (n - 0.5)(cell - 0.5) --- pixels are there for certain, which is that over the cell in columns. It --- may give up a column or two that would have fit; it never draws past the --- edge. With no cell width to go on, one column comes off, as before. --- --- The main console (nil) is drawn at the default, and so is a window not --- there yet, for which getColumnCount raises. function M.width(win) if win then local ok, n = pcall(getColumnCount, win) if ok and type(n) == "number" and n > 1 then local cell = M.cellWidth(win) if cell and cell > 1 then return math.max(20, math.floor((n - 0.5) * (cell - 0.5) / cell)) end return math.max(20, math.floor(n) - 1) end end return M.DEFAULT_WIDTH end --- Draw the pieces M.render made into a window, or the main console for nil. function M.draw(win) for _, piece in ipairs(M.render(M.width(win))) do if type(piece) == "table" then if win then cechoLink(win, piece[1], piece[2], piece[3], true) else cechoLink(piece[1], piece[2], piece[3], true) end else if win then cecho(win, piece) else cecho(piece) end end end end
--- Open the window, or show it again if it was closed. No dock area is --- given: Mudlet docks a new window on the right by itself, and given one it --- re-docks a window that already exists, every time, squeezing it into the --- right dock even when the player had floated or sized it elsewhere, and --- every click on a set name comes through here. function M.open() openUserWindow(M.WINDOW, true, true) pcall(setUserWindowTitle, M.WINDOW, "Talismans") S.opened = true end
--- Draw what is known into the window. It is opened only the first time, --- since openUserWindow on an existing window shows it, and a window closed --- with its own X should stay closed until asked for again; drawing into a --- closed one is harmless and keeps it current for then. function M.redraw() if not M.data.shown then return false end if not S.opened then M.open() end -- A user window wraps at a fixed column, not at its edge, so a layout as -- wide as the window would otherwise fold where that column falls. S.drawnWidth = M.width(M.WINDOW) pcall(setWindowWrap, M.WINDOW, S.drawnWidth) clearWindow(M.WINDOW) M.draw(M.WINDOW) return true end
-- How long a resize has to settle before the window is laid out again: -- dragging an edge raises the event at every step of the drag. M.RESIZE_WAIT = 0.25
--- Lay the window out again once it has been resized to a different number --- of columns. function M.onResize(_, _, _, name) if name ~= M.WINDOW or not M.data.shown then return false end if S.resizeTimer then pcall(killTimer, S.resizeTimer) end S.resizeTimer = tempTimer(M.RESIZE_WAIT, function() S.resizeTimer = nil if M.width(M.WINDOW) ~= S.drawnWidth then M.redraw() end end) return true end
-- ------------------------------------------------------------------- scanning
-- A scan sends one command, waits for its output to be read, and only then -- sends the next, so two outputs never arrive tangled and the game is never -- flooded. One that has not answered in this long is given up on. M.SCAN_WAIT = 8
local function scanSend() local scan = S.scan local step = table.remove(scan.queue, 1) if not step then S.scan = nil log(M.scanSummary(scan)) return end scan.step = step send(step.cmd, false) scan.timer = tempTimer(M.SCAN_WAIT, function() M.scanTimeout() end) end
local function infoFor(list) local steps = {} for _, tkw in ipairs(list) do steps[#steps + 1] = { cmd = "talisman info " .. tkw, kind = "info", kw = tkw } end return steps end
--- Pieces held, counted as the game lists them (a level-5 piece is one), --- of every talisman, or of one set's talismans only. function M.piecesHeld(setKw) local inSet if setKw then inSet = {} local set = M.data.sets[setKw] for _, t in ipairs(set and set.talismans or {}) do inSet[t.kw] = true end end local n = 0 for _, row in ipairs(M.data.held) do if not inSet or inSet[row.group or M.ownerOf(row.kw) or ""] then n = n + (row.count or 1) end end return n end
--- The line a scan ends on: what it found, and every step the game never --- answered, since those lines were not hidden but are easily missed. function M.scanSummary(scan) local n = M.piecesHeld(scan.set) local found = n .. (n == 1 and " piece" or " pieces") .. " found" if scan.set then local set = M.data.sets[scan.set] found = found .. " for " .. (set and set.name or scan.set) end local line = "Scan completed (" .. found .. ")" if #scan.unanswered > 0 then line = line .. ". <red>Not answered: " .. table.concat(scan.unanswered, ", ") .. "<reset>" end return line end
function M.scan(setKw) -- One at a time. A second would leave the first's listing half read and -- on the screen, and a double click on [scan] would send everything twice. if S.scan then log("A scan is already running; `tals stop` ends it") return false end -- Whatever was half read before is not what the scan will be waiting for. S.cap, S.paging, S.answered = nil, false, false endTail() local queue, set if setKw and setKw ~= "" then setKw = setKw:lower() set = setKw -- PIECES as well, so the count it ends on is one it read. Its INFO -- steps are added after this, once SET says which talismans to ask for. queue = { { cmd = "talisman set " .. setKw, kind = "set", then_ = "setInfo" }, { cmd = "talisman pieces", kind = "pieces" }, } log("Scan started (set " .. setKw .. ")") M.data.focus = M.data.sets[setKw] and setKw or M.data.focus else -- LIST rather than SETS: it prints the same sets table, after the -- talismans you have done, which is the only place those are listed. queue = { -- After LIST, SET for every set it listed: the only listing that says -- which talismans a set holds, and so the marks beside each set. { cmd = "talisman list", kind = "sets", kinds = { tlist = true }, then_ = "allSets" }, { cmd = "talisman pieces", kind = "pieces", then_ = "heldInfo" }, } log("Scan started") end S.scan = { queue = queue, heard = 0, missed = 0, unanswered = {}, set = set } scanSend() return true end
--- Whether the scan's step in flight is waiting for this capture. function M.scanWaitsFor(cap) local step = S.scan and S.scan.step if not (step and step.kind == cap.kind) then return false end -- INFO for some other talisman, typed meanwhile, is not the answer. return not step.kw or cap.kw == step.kw end
--- A capture was read; if the scan was waiting for one like it, move on. function M.scanHeard(cap) local scan = S.scan if not M.scanWaitsFor(cap) then return false end if scan.timer then pcall(killTimer, scan.timer); scan.timer = nil end scan.heard = scan.heard + 1 local after = scan.step.then_ if after == "allSets" then -- Before the INFO steps, which PIECES adds after this. Each SET records -- its talismans and nothing more: INFO for every talisman of every set -- would be hundreds of commands. for _, kw in ipairs(M.data.setOrder) do scan.queue[#scan.queue + 1] = { cmd = "talisman set " .. kw, kind = "set" } end elseif after == "heldInfo" then local todo = {} for _, tkw in ipairs(M.heldTalismans()) do if not M.data.talismans[tkw] then todo[#todo + 1] = tkw end end for _, step in ipairs(infoFor(todo)) do scan.queue[#scan.queue + 1] = step end elseif after == "setInfo" then local list = {} for _, t in ipairs(cap.rows or {}) do list[#list + 1] = t.kw end for _, step in ipairs(infoFor(list)) do scan.queue[#scan.queue + 1] = step end M.data.focus = cap.key or cap.kw -- SET's own keyword for the set, which the one typed may cut short. scan.set = M.data.focus M.save() end scan.step = nil scanSend() return true end
function M.scanTimeout() local scan = S.scan if not scan then return end scan.timer = nil scan.missed = scan.missed + 1 -- A page it answered and never saw continued (a disconnect between the -- MORE and its answer) is not the scan's any more: its prompts are shown. S.answered = false if scan.step then scan.unanswered[#scan.unanswered + 1] = scan.step.cmd end scan.step = nil scanSend() end
function M.stopScan(quiet) local scan = S.scan if not scan then return false end if scan.timer then pcall(killTimer, scan.timer) end S.scan = nil S.answered = false if not quiet then log("Scan stopped") end return true end
-- ------------------------------------------------------------------ commands
-- How long a typed `TALISMAN PIECES <t>` names the talisman for the output -- that answers it. M.ASKED_FOR = 10
--- Every command sent, whoever sent it: kept only when it asks for one --- talisman's pieces, since that output does not say whose they are. function M.onSend(cmd) if type(cmd) ~= "string" then return end -- Either word may be cut short to three letters or more, in case the game -- takes that (`tal pie`); the full words are what is captured. Only real -- beginnings of the two words count, so `talk pie bob` does not. local a, b, kw = cmd:lower():match("^%s*(%a+)%s+(%a+)%s+(%S+)%s*$") if not a or #a < 3 or #b < 3 then return end if ("talisman"):sub(1, #a) ~= a or ("pieces"):sub(1, #b) ~= b then return end S.asked = { kw = kw, at = M.now() } end
--- A talisman keyword as typed, which may be cut short (`silver` for --- `silverdragon`), resolved against the keywords already known: itself if --- known, else the one known keyword it starts, else itself as typed when it --- starts none. Nil when it could be more than one. function M.resolveTalisman(kw) local known = {} for tkw in pairs(M.data.talismans) do known[tkw] = true end for _, row in ipairs(M.data.held) do if row.group then known[row.group] = true end end for _, set in pairs(M.data.sets) do for _, t in ipairs(set.talismans or {}) do known[t.kw] = true end end if known[kw] then return kw end local found for tkw in pairs(known) do if tkw:sub(1, #kw) == kw then if found then return nil end found = tkw end end return found or kw end
function M.setFocus(kw) M.data.focus = (kw or ""):lower() M.show(true) return M.data.focus end
-- What follows `tals ` in each of build.py's aliases, as Lua patterns: the -- same forms, and case-sensitive like them. The harness holds the two -- together. --- Fold one talisman to its name, or list its pieces. function M.toggleTalisman(kw) M.data.openTalismans[kw] = (not M.data.openTalismans[kw]) or nil M.save() M.redraw() return M.data.openTalismans[kw] == true end
